test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 30 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: How many cities were covered under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) by June 2025 to combat air pollution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**131**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)** is a long-term, time-bound, national-level strategy to tackle the air pollution problem across India in a comprehensive manner.
 
• By **June 2025**, the total number of cities covered under this flagship program is **131**.
 
• These cities are primarily identified as **non-attainment cities**, which means they did not meet the **National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS)** for five consecutive years.
 
• The program initially started with **102 cities** in **2019**, which was later expanded to **122**, and eventually to **131** cities to include those receiving grants under the **XV Finance Commission** for million-plus population cities.
 
• The primary objective of covering these **131 cities** is to implement city-specific action plans to reduce the levels of **Particulate Matter (PM10 and PM2.5)** significantly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Launch and Governance:**
 
 
• The **NCAP** was launched in **January 2019** by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)**.
 
• It represents the first such effort in **India** to frame a national framework for air quality management with a time-bound reduction target.
 
 
 
• **Revised Targets:**
 
 
• Initially, the goal was to achieve a **20% to 30% reduction** in particulate matter concentration by **2024** (with **2017** as the base year).
 
• In **September 2022**, the Government of India updated the goal to a **40% reduction** in particulate matter levels or achieving the **National Ambient Air Quality Standards** by **2025-26**.
 
 
 
• **PRANA Portal:**
 
 
• To monitor the progress of the program in these **131 cities**, the government launched **PRANA (Portal for Regulation of Air-pollution in Non-Attainment cities)**.
 
• This portal tracks the physical and financial status of city action plan implementation and disseminates information on air quality to the public.
 
 
 
• **Funding Mechanisms:**
 
 
• Funding for the program is funneled through the **Control of Pollution** scheme for **82 cities** with a population below one million.
 
• For the remaining **49 cities** (million-plus cities), funding is provided through the **XV Finance Commission** air quality grants.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Multi-Sectoral Approach:** The **NCAP** focuses on various sources of pollution, including **industrial emissions**, **vehicular exhaust**, **biomass burning**, and **construction dust**.
 
• **Institutional Framework:** It involves collaboration between the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)**, **State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs)**, and **Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)** to ensure ground-level execution of clean air plans.
 
• **Monitoring Stations:** As part of the program, there has been a significant increase in the number of **Manual Monitoring Stations** and **Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Stations (CAAQMS)** across the **131 identified cities** to provide real-time data.
 
• **Base Year:** The base year for measuring the concentration of pollutants and calculating the percentage of reduction is **2017**.
